taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Chthamalia biflora and treats Matelea biflora as a synonym. Flora of North America 2023 uses Matelea biflora as an alternative accepted treatment; the project canonical name follows current Kew.
look_here_first: Look for a low, densely hairy plant with dark maroon-to-brown star-shaped flowers, commonly paired close to the stem and heart-shaped leaves. Then inspect the milkweed gynostegium in the flower center.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — UT PRC Purola Preserve records Matelea biflora, a synonym of current Kew Chthamalia biflora, as naturally occurring. Travis — UT PRC Travis County herbarium records Matelea biflora under the same species concept. Kerr — TPWD Kerr Wildlife Management Area flora records Matelea biflora.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: No county inferred from statewide or ecoregion range. Legacy Matelea/Gonolobus names are counted only where the species concept is reconciled.

best_field_traits: low decumbent or trailing herb, often about 7–40 cm
stems and leaves densely hirsute with long hairs plus minute glandular hairs
maroon to dark-brown non-reticulate rotate-campanulate corolla
corolla lobes commonly reflexed and hairy on the inner surface
five-part ring corona with incurved appendages arching over the anthers
central gynostegium conspicuous at close range
plant may be noticeably malodorous when handled
joey_field_notes: Joey's Edwards Plateau video shows the dark hairy maroon flower and discusses its dark color and hairs in the context of possible fly/fungus-gnat pollination.
In a close-up, Joey explicitly corrects the central milkweed reproductive column to 'gynostegium,' making this a high-value structural teaching frame.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Pearl milkvine is a longer twining vine with broad pale-green strongly net-reticulate flowers and a silvery center. Matelea edwardsensis is a twining vine with pale green campanulate flowers marked mostly by longitudinal lines. Chthamalia biflora stays low and densely hairy and has paired dark non-reticulate flowers.
